[
  {"sentence": 1, "status": "present", "evidence": "Prologue: on the sinking Lusitania a frightened man gives an American girl an oilskin packet of 'vitally important papers' because of 'women and children first.' Carter later names him Danvers and the girl Jane Finn.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 2, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Tommy, old thing!' 'Tuppence, old bean!' at the Dover Street Tube; Tommy demobbed; Tuppence the 'fifth daughter of Archdeacon Cowley' who worked in a hospital.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 3, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Tommy, you're stony!'; both job-hunting; 'Let's be adventurers!'; 'The Young Adventurers, Ltd.!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 4, "status": "present", "evidence": "Whittington: 'I happened to overhear part of your conversation'; offers £100 to enter a Paris pensionnat as his ward.", "note": "Carter later explains she was to pose as Jane Finn."},
  {"sentence": 5, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Jane Finn,' she said hastily. Whittington is purple with rage and dismay and gives her 'fifty to go on with.' Next day the office is closed and Whittington has gone; Tommy says 'I told it to you.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 6, "status": "present", "evidence": "'The advertisement has appeared, and--there are only two answers!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 7, "status": "present", "evidence": "First letter is signed 'A. CARTER.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 8."},
  {"sentence": 8, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Yes, sir, I recognized you at once. Saw you in France when I was with the Intelligence'; 'he's IT!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 9, "status": "present", "evidence": "Carter explains the draft treaty and that Jane Finn vanished. It 'undoubtedly implicates a number of our statesmen'; 'Bolshevist gold is pouring into this country to procure a Revolution'; there is a 'strike menace.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 10, "status": "present", "evidence": "'He is always spoken of by the unassuming title of \"Mr. Brown.\"'", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 11."},
  {"sentence": 11, "status": "present", "evidence": "'a certain man, whose real name is unknown to us'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 12, "status": "present", "evidence": "'How would you like to work for me?... Find Jane Finn.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 13, "status": "present", "evidence": "Second letter signed 'JULIUS P. HERSHEIMMER.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 14."},
  {"sentence": 14, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius says Jane is his cousin. 'Inspector Brown' took the only photograph, and 'no such person... was known to Scotland Yard.' This brings 'a rapprochement between Julius Hersheimmer and the Young Adventurers.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 15, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence reasons that Danvers was shadowed, probably by a woman, and that this may have been 'Rita'; they search the Lusitania survivors list.", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 16."},
  {"sentence": 16, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Mrs. Vandemeyer, 20 South Audley Mansions'; 'She's mostly called that [Rita], sir, but Marguerite's her name.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 17, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tommy follows Boris to a Soho house, copies the knock and says 'Mr. Brown?', and is told 'Upstairs.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 18."},
  {"sentence": 18, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tommy overhears the meeting from the next room. Number One, later identified as Kramenin, takes the head of the table. 'And--the date, my friend?' 'The 29th.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 19, "status": "present", "evidence": "'A crashing blow descended on his head'; Tommy then bargains: 'I don't know where the papers are--but I believe that I can find them.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 20, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence recruits the lift-boy Albert, who arranges the place for her.", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 21."},
  {"sentence": 21, "status": "present", "evidence": "Hired as house-parlourmaid under the name 'Prudence Cooper.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 22, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Sir James Peel Edgerton. This, then, was the famous K.C.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 23."},
  {"sentence": 23, "status": "present", "evidence": "'a change does no harm sometimes... Just a hint.' He later agrees to help find Tommy.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 24, "status": "present", "evidence": "Mrs. Vandemeyer puts 'a rim of cold steel' to Tuppence's temple.", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentences 25 and 26."},
  {"sentence": 25, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence seizes the revolver and offers 'a hundred thousand' from 'an American millionaire.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 26, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Who is Mr. Brown?'; Mrs. Vandemeyer agrees: 'I'll do it.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 27, "status": "present", "evidence": "She faints on seeing Sir James and Julius in the doorway. They keep a vigil, and in the morning she is dead; there is 'an odour of chloral' and the bottle is empty.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 28, "status": "present", "evidence": "Dr. Hall says 'Janet Vandemeyer' was placed at his Bournemouth home suffering 'complete loss of memory,' but 'Miss Vandemeyer is no longer under my care.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 29, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius proposes. Tuppence later cries 'Oh, Tommy... I do love you so.' Her note says 'Let's leave it till then.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 30, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Come at once, Moat House, Ebury, Yorkshire, great developments--TOMMY.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 31, "status": "present", "evidence": "Annette slips Tommy a penknife and helps him escape, crying 'I want to go back to Marguerite.' At the Ritz he learns Miss Cowley has gone out.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 32, "status": "present", "evidence": "'A week! We're no nearer to finding Tuppence.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 33, "status": "present", "evidence": "Telegram: 'Jane Finn found. Come Manchester... PEEL EDGERTON.' The girl recalls the hiding place, and Tommy and Julius find the packet on the cliff path. The sheet reads 'WITH THE COMPLIMENTS OF MR. BROWN.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 34."},
  {"sentence": 34, "status": "present", "evidence": "A green toque and a coat marked P.L.C. are 'washed up on the Yorkshire coast.' Tommy shouts at Julius: 'I loved her... Tuppence is my girl!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 35, "status": "present", "evidence": "'What on earth was a photograph of the French girl Annette doing in Julius Hersheimmer's writing-table?' His letter to Carter says 'that girl at Manchester was just a plant.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 36, "status": "present", "evidence": "'I kept my mind open between the two of them.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 37."},
  {"sentence": 37, "status": "present", "evidence": "He leaves Julius a note about going to the Argentine and drops Sir James's letter by the desk. The true telegram reads 'Astley Priors, Gatehouse, Kent.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 38, "status": "present", "evidence": "Note signed 'TWOPENCE'; 'She'd never spell her name \"Twopence\"... Julius had seen it... but Sir James hadn't!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 39, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius holds Kramenin at gunpoint and makes him bring the girls out of Astley Priors. Annette: 'Been fooling them all the time, eh?' Jane: 'Five years! Five long years!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 40, "status": "present", "evidence": "'That's why I sent the girls off to Sir James... I was sure they'd fetch up at the house in Soho.' The papers are behind the picture of Marguerite in the Faust room.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 41, "status": "present", "evidence": "Jane extracts the two sheets from behind the picture. Sir James says 'I am Mr. Brown' and raises his automatic.", "note": "Sentence fragment, continued in sentence 42."},
  {"sentence": 42, "status": "present", "evidence": "He is 'seized from behind in a grip of iron' by Julius and Tommy, who had hidden behind the curtain in the recess.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 43, "status": "present", "evidence": "'the hand which bore the big signet ring, was raised to his lips'; 'an odour of bitter almonds filled the air.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 44, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Deprived of their chief, the organization fell to pieces.' The draft treaty is 'reduced to ashes.' 'It was to be Peace, not War!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 45, "status": "present", "evidence": "At the Savoy supper Carter reads from the brown diary. Sir William tells Tommy 'let bygones be bygones... You're my heir.' Carter toasts Jane as 'one of the bravest of America's daughters!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 46, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius proposes to Jane in the car and she answers 'I love you now, Julius.' In a taxi, Tommy and Tuppence agree to marry ('Ours, so there!').", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 47, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Marriage... do you know what I think it is?' 'A sport!' Carter also credits Tommy's dogged common sense in defeating the master criminal.", "note": "The theme is conveyed implicitly through the outcome."}
]
